text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SLO breach: streaming p99 > 3.0s in region eu-west-2 — triggered at 1932000123. Affected service: streaming-api (route /v1/stream). Escalation: paging Kaela (oncall). :rotating_light:

Kaela (oncall): I'm on it, paging into #incidents. Initial check: dashboards show p95 ~ 750ms, p99 ~ 3.2s, error rate stable. Streaming tail stalls increasing ~15% of sessions.

Leah (SRE): seeing same, tail latency jumps align with NAT gateway egress spikes and some TLS handshake spikes. Adding NetEng.

Tom (NetEng): looking at VPC flows — there's intermittent retransmit and queueing on the egress path between az-b and az-c. Could be mesh-egress queuing on the GW nodes.

Matt (Infra): rolling through gateway pod metrics now, CPU/RX/TX look fine, but tx-queue depth on host NIC shows sustained growth during spikes.

Sanjay (API): customer impact — CS reports 3 customers with high-volume streams complaining about stalls and reconnects; Nina is pulling customer logs.

Nina (Customer Success): confirmed, 2 enterprise tenants and 1 high-traffic startup. They're seeing repeated stalls ~2-5s then resume. Will notify them we are investigating.

Kaela (oncall): checklist run: dependency health (ok), model hosts healthy, controller pods ok. Networking seems implicated. Can we get conntrack and NAT metrics?

Tom (NetEng): pulling conntrack counts and SNAT stats now. Quick outputs:

```
# conntrack -S | grep entries
entries: 12456  # baseline ~6k, spike coincides with incident
# ip -s link show gw0
TX queue length: 1024 -> growing to 4096 during spike
# aws natgw-metrics --region eu-west-2 --metric BytesOut
spike window: +48% in egress throughput
```

Leah (SRE): conntrack doubled, SNAT translations increased, observed per-host ephemeral port allocation close to limits on several NAT gateways. But not full exhaustion. Packet retransmit rate between AZs up ~4x.

Matt (Infra): I can scale the egress fleet and spin up an extra NAT gateway in az-c to redistribute. Do we want an automated route shift to prefer az-a/az-b?

Kaela (oncall): Do it. Prefer redistributing to az-a and az-b where we see lower queueing. Matt, spin new natgw in az-c and add to rotation; update route table weighting. Tom, can you confirm no BGP flaps?

Tom (NetEng): BGP stable. I will adjust subnet egress weighting. Also adding iptables conntrack-timeout tweak to reduce stale entries for short-lived streams (small experiment).

Sanjay (API): Can we enable streaming fallback to model-smaller variant and reduce max chunk size for affected customers while we stabilize network? Would reduce per-session bandwidth and help queueing.

Kaela (oncall): Good idea. SREs, deploy controlled fallback for tenants flagged by Nina. Use canary feature flag for 5% of flows first.

Leah (SRE): rolling canary now. Command run in control plane:

```bash
# rollout: feature-flag stream-egress-fallback -> 5%
redwoodctl feature set stream-egress-fallback --percent 5 --selector region=eu-west-2
```

Leah (SRE): canary checked, initial 5% shows p99 down from 3.2s -> 1.8s for those flows. No errors.

Tom (NetEng): route weighting update completed, new natgw added in az-c, and host tx-queue tuning applied on the GW hosts. Conntrack timeout change applied to 60s for RELATED state.

Matt (Infra): egress fleet scaled +30% in eu-west-2. NIC tx-queue growth stopped, retransmit dropped ~70% from peak.

Kaela (oncall): monitoring — p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 1.9s, streaming stall rate down to ~4%. Still above target but trending. Continuing mitigation.

Sanjay (API): notifying affected customers with mitigation summary. Nina, tag customers for follow-up and extended credits if needed.

Nina (Customer Success): doing that now. Draft msg: "We're investigating a transient networking congestion in eu-west-2 affecting streaming; temporary fallbacks and routing changes applied; we'll follow up with root cause and crediting details." Will send after you approve.

Leah (SRE): collecting packet captures from GW nodes and pcap aggregated from affected proxy pods. Snippet from tcpdump shows repeated TLS handshake retransmits and 0-byte TCP segments during queue spikes.

```
15:23:12.123 IP client > gw: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
15:23:12.343 IP gw > client: Flags [S.], ack 1, options (mss 1460), length 0
15:23:15.678 IP client > gw: Flags [P.], seq 1:145, ack 1, length 144
# large RTT spikes visible in pcap
```

Tom (NetEng): hypothesis: mesh egress queueing + conntrack growth caused retransmits and TLS handshake tail spikes. Root cause likely backlog on egress NIC due to bursty high-throughput customers hitting same egress path.

Kaela (oncall): next actions: 1) keep scaled egress until next sitrep, 2) widen fallback to 20% if p99 doesn't return <1.5s in 15m, 3) gather metrics for postmortem: conntrack growth patterns, NAT translation distribution, route weighting changes, pcap.

Matt (Infra): putting a 2-hour temporary autoscale policy on natgw pool in eu-west-2 to keep capacity elevated.

Sanjay (API): preparing post-incident customer note template.

Nina (Customer Success): sent interim comms to impacted tenants. They ack'd and asked for ETA. Told them 2-3h while we verify.

Kaela (oncall): current status at 1932000765: mitigation in place, partial recovery observed. Keeping this thread open for postmortem data collection. If p99 holds under 2s for 30m we'll move to monitoring and then postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
